summaries.gardner: Altria fits few Rule Breaker traits: it is a mature incumbent in a shrinking US cigarette market, not a top dog in an important emerging industry, and its smoke-free efforts trail PMI's ZYN and IQOS. It does show strong recent price momentum (up 36.6% year to date to mid-October 2026) and has a consumer brand in Marlboro, but it is led by a newly appointed career finance executive and is not commonly seen as overvalued by its enthusiasts.
summaries.buffett: Altria has several Buffett traits: a simple business, Marlboro's brand and pricing power, 72.2% gross margins and 2025 free cash flow of $9,074M, all paid out to owners through a 61-times-raised dividend and buybacks. Against it are a product in long-term volume decline, negative shareholders' equity and $24.6B of debt, and a record of poor capital allocation (the $12.8B JUUL stake and the NJOY write-downs); at about 13 times forward earnings the price is reasonable but a conservative DCF gives no margin of safety.
summaries.munger: Munger would see an easy-to-understand franchise with real pricing power, but inverting shows many ways it could weaken: falling cigarette volumes, an FDA proposal to cap nicotine, litigation, illicit vapes and losing the smoke-free shift to stronger rivals. Its expensive JUUL and NJOY bets are the kind of capital-allocation errors Munger warned against, and the tobacco business is one he and Buffett avoided for ethical reasons.
summaries.lynch: Altria is a classic Lynch slow grower bought for its dividend (a 6%-plus yield, raised 61 times in 57 years), with a simple story of price rises offsetting falling volumes and steady buybacks. Its forward P/E of about 13 is well above its roughly 4-5% expected EPS growth, so it fails Lynch's PEG test, and it is widely followed rather than overlooked.
summaries.fisher: Altria scores poorly on Fisher's points: revenues net of excise have slipped from $20,841M (2020) to $20,139M (2025), and its attempts at new products (JUUL, NJOY ACE, IQOS in the US) have largely failed or been sold. It does have strong margins and a disciplined cost base, but Fisher looked for companies with sales growth potential for years, which Altria lacks.
summaries.graham: Altria passes several of Graham's defensive tests: it is large, has paid dividends for decades, grew diluted EPS 54% from $2.67 (2015) to $4.12 (2025) and trades at about 14.8 times its 2023-2025 average EPS. It fails on earnings stability (a $1,293M net loss in 2019) and on financial condition, with negative book value, a current ratio of about 0.5 and debt far above cash.
summaries.thiel: Altria does not fit Thiel's framework: it has no proprietary technology, operates in a shrinking market it has dominated for decades, and is not riding a new technology wave. Its strengths are distribution and a regulated market that deters entrants, but its position in the growing smoke-free categories is weak.
summaries.gerstner: Altria is far from a Gerstner-style investment: there is no AI or other secular growth tailwind, revenue is flat to declining and the stock's appeal is yield rather than compounding growth. Its cost discipline and capital returns fit his calls for efficiency, but he favours durable growth at a reasonable price, which Altria does not offer.
summaries.druckenmiller: Druckenmiller looks for accelerating earnings and catalysts with liquidity behind them; Altria offers steady low-single-digit adjusted EPS growth (2026 guidance $5.61-$5.72, up 3.5%-5.5%) and missed consensus in two of the last four quarters. Its strong 2026 share price run is a momentum point in its favour, but there is no clear earnings inflection to support a large position.
summaries.smith: Altria partly fits Terry Smith's 'good company' test, with very high returns on capital (ROIC about 46%), 72% gross margins and strong cash conversion, and Fundsmith has itself owned tobacco stocks. But Smith also wants growth he can reinvest at high returns, and Altria's sales are shrinking and its reinvestments (JUUL, NJOY) have destroyed value.
summaries.greenblatt: On the Magic Formula Altria scores well on return on capital (about 46%) and reasonably on earnings yield, with 2025 operating income of $9,899M equal to about 6.7% of its $147.6B enterprise value. That makes it a respectable but not top-ranked Magic Formula candidate.
summaries.akre: Akre's three-legged stool needs a great business, skilled and honest management and the ability to reinvest at high rates; Altria has the first in part (Marlboro's pricing power and margins) but not the third, since almost all cash goes to dividends and buybacks. Management under new CEO Sal Mancuso is competent and shareholder-oriented but has a weak record on reinvestment.
summaries.pabrai: Altria fits Pabrai's preference for simple, durable businesses and its 7.2% free-cash-flow yield limits downside, but it is not a distressed bargain facing a temporary problem: its volume decline is structural. With the price above most analyst targets, it does not offer the 'heads I win, tails I don't lose much' set-up he seeks.
summaries.wood: Altria is the opposite of an ARK disruptive-innovation investment: it sells a mature, declining product and is not a leader in AI, robotics, energy storage, blockchain or genomics. Its smoke-free products are incremental and lag rivals', so it falls outside Cathie Wood's framework.
summaries.ackman: Altria partly fits Ackman's criteria of a simple, predictable, free-cash-flow-generative business with high barriers to entry and limited exposure to commodity prices. However, he also looks for a growing business with a strong balance sheet, whereas Altria's revenues are slowly falling and it carries $24.6B of debt with negative equity.
summaries.sleep: Nick Sleep favoured companies that share scale economies with customers and grow stronger over time; Altria does the opposite, raising prices each year as volumes fall. Its position in 10-20 years looks weaker rather than stronger as smokers quit or move to rivals' smoke-free products.
summaries.valentine: Valentine looked for huge markets being created by new technology; Altria serves a shrinking market with old products. Smoke-free nicotine is a sizeable opportunity, but Altria is a follower there rather than the company creating the market.
summaries.nash: Altria fails most of Tom Nash's tests: revenue is shrinking, debt ($24,577M) far exceeds cash ($2,367M), it missed EPS consensus in two of the last four quarters and it faces major regulatory and legal threats. Its strengths are a 49% operating margin, a 45% free-cash-flow margin and low short interest, but its score on Nash's 13 categories (about 45 of 130) and a DCF value of about $43 a share at 12% are far below his thresholds.

momentum.evidence: The share price rose 36.6% year to date to Oct 14, 2026 versus 12.5% for SPY (Trefis), and 15.8% over the last 52 weeks to $75.11 (StockAnalysis, Oct 16, 2026), plus a dividend yield of about 6%.

g4.evidence: Altria is led by Sal Mancuso, a career finance executive who became CEO in May 2026, and is held mainly by index and income funds (65% institutional ownership) rather than backed by famous visionary investors or partners.

g6.evidence: The stock trades above the analysts' average target of $70 and median of $71 (14 analysts, consensus Hold, StockAnalysis, Oct 14, 2026), but at about 13 times forward earnings it is generally described as cheap rather than overvalued.

simple.evidence: Altria sells Marlboro cigarettes, Copenhagen and Skoal smokeless tobacco, on! nicotine pouches and NJOY vapes in the US, a business easy for a generalist to understand.

b2.evidence: Revenues net of excise have been flat to slightly down ($20,841M in 2020 to $20,139M in 2025) and reported EPS swings with impairments (a 2019 net loss of $1,293M), but the dividend has been raised 61 times in 57 years.

integrity.evidence: Altria reports clearly and returns nearly all cash to shareholders, but large capital-allocation mistakes (the $12.8B JUUL investment, largely written off, and $2.1B of e-vapor write-downs in 2025) and an insider ownership of only 0.08% weigh against it.

b6.evidence: Altria followed industry trends with costly deals such as the $12.8B JUUL stake (2018), a Cronos cannabis stake and the 2023 NJOY purchase, much of which has been written down.

roic.evidence: Return on invested capital is about 46% (StockAnalysis, Oct 2026), but Altria relies heavily on debt: $24,577M of debt against $2,367M of cash and negative shareholders' equity of $2,618M at June 30, 2026.

fcf.evidence: In 2025 operating cash flow of $9,290M less capital expenditures of $216M gave free cash flow of $9,074M, 131% of net earnings of $6,947M (which were reduced by non-cash impairments).

b10.evidence: Altria pays out nearly all earnings (dividends of $6,960M in 2025 against net earnings of $6,947M), and the capital it did keep was largely lost on the JUUL and NJOY investments.

safety.evidence: At $75.11 the stock trades above a conservative DCF value of about $43 a share (12% discount rate; about $61 at 10%) and above the analysts' average target of $70, so there is no margin of safety.

fairprice.evidence: About 13.2 times 2026 consensus adjusted EPS of $5.68 is modest and far below PMI's roughly 23 times, but it pays for expected EPS growth of only about 4.7% and slowly falling revenue.

mu5.evidence: Nicotine demand is sticky and the brand is entrenched, but cigarette volumes are falling steeply (shipments down 10.0% in 2025), and an FDA nicotine cap, litigation, excise taxes, illicit vapes and $24.6B of debt are several ways the business could be impaired.

reinvest.evidence: Capital spending is small ($216M in 2025) and almost all cash goes to dividends and buybacks; its main reinvestments (JUUL, NJOY) produced large write-downs.

ly2.evidence: Altria is a clear slow grower: a high-dividend company whose story is price increases and buybacks offsetting falling cigarette volumes, with adjusted EPS guided up 3.5%-5.5% in 2026.

ly3.evidence: At $75.11 Altria trades at about 18.2 times 2025 reported diluted EPS of $4.12 and about 13.2 times 2026 consensus adjusted EPS of $5.68, well above that estimate's 4.7% growth.

runway.evidence: Revenues net of excise have fallen in four of the last five years and analysts expect roughly flat revenue to 2030 (TickFlow FY2030 average $20.60B vs $20,139M in 2025).

ly7.evidence: Diluted shares fell from 1,859M (2020) to 1,683M (2025) through buybacks ($335M in the first half of 2026), and insiders bought 1,500 shares in the last three months, but insiders were net sellers of about 34,000 shares over 18 months (GuruFocus).

ly8.evidence: Tobacco is a 'boring', ESG-shunned industry, but Altria is a $125B company covered by 14 analysts with 65% institutional ownership, so it is not overlooked.

fi2.evidence: Altria is developing smoke-free products such as on! PLUS (national expansion planned for Q3 2026) and NJOY, but NJOY ACE is off the market after an ITC patent ruling and it sold its US IQOS rights to PMI in 2024.

fi3.evidence: Its new-product spending and investments have produced few winners: on!'s share of nicotine pouches fell to 14.4% in Q2 2026, NJOY ACE was barred, and e-vapor assets were written down by $2.1B in 2025.

fi4.evidence: Strong retail programs keep Marlboro at 59.4% of the premium cigarette segment (2025) despite marketing restrictions, but Altria has failed to win share in pouches and vapes against ZYN and illicit disposables.

longterm.evidence: Management states a vision to move adult smokers to a smoke-free future, but most profit still comes from raising cigarette prices and nearly all cash is paid out rather than invested in innovation.

gr1.evidence: Altria had net revenues of $23,279M in 2025 and a market value of about $125B in October 2026.

ni10.evidence: Altria reported a net loss of $1,293M in 2019 (JUUL impairment), although it was profitable in the other nine years from 2016 to 2025, including $6,947M in 2025.

gr4.evidence: Altria has paid a dividend continuously for decades and in August 2026 announced its 61st dividend increase in 57 years, to $1.11 a quarter.

eps10.evidence: Reported diluted EPS rose 54% from $2.67 in 2015 to $4.12 in 2025.

gr6.evidence: At $75.11 the stock is about 14.8 times its three-year average diluted EPS of $5.08 ($4.57, $6.54 and $4.12 in 2023-2025), though 2024 was boosted by the IQOS rights sale.

gr7.evidence: Altria has negative book value (shareholders' deficit of $2,618M at June 30, 2026), so P/E times P/B cannot meet Graham's 22.5 limit.

th1.evidence: Altria has no proprietary technology that is ten times better; its cigarettes, pouches and vapes have close substitutes, and NJOY ACE was barred over a patent dispute with JUUL.

timing.evidence: The timing works against it: smokers are leaving cigarettes for smoke-free products where rivals such as ZYN and illicit vapes lead, and Altria guides that NJOY ACE will not return in 2026.

th3.evidence: Altria did not start with a small niche; Marlboro has long held a large share of a big US cigarette market that is now shrinking.

team.evidence: CEO Sal Mancuso, a career finance executive who became CEO in May 2026, is an experienced manager rather than an exceptional founder or proven world-class team.

th5.evidence: Altria has deep relationships with US wholesalers and convenience-store retailers and trade programs that put its products in front of adult nicotine users nationwide.

durable.evidence: Regulation and brand loyalty protect Marlboro, but falling cigarette volumes, rising discount share and weak smoke-free positions make its market position over 10-20 years uncertain.

th7.evidence: Altria has not found a unique opportunity others miss; the smoke-free shift is pursued by all major tobacco firms and it is a follower there.

trend.evidence: Altria is not a beneficiary of a major platform shift; it is the incumbent being disrupted by the move to smoke-free nicotine.

tn20.evidence: Over the last five quarters Altria beat twice (Q2 2025, Q1 2026), was in line once (Q3 2025) and missed twice (Q4 2025 $1.30 vs $1.32; Q2 2026 $1.48 vs $1.50) (247 Wall St).

tn21.evidence: There is no sign of fraud, a co-CEO, an auditor change (PwC) or an acquisition spree, but reported operating margin has declined from 52.2% in 2020 to 49.2% in 2025 because of impairments.

tn22.evidence: Altria has $20.1B of revenue net of excise, strong profits and cash flow, and buys back rather than sells shares.

tn24.evidence: With trailing free cash flow of about $9.1B, a 12% discount rate and 4% terminal growth, the $75.11 price implies about 9% annual free-cash-flow growth for five years, while revenue is shrinking about 1% a year.

tn25.evidence: Using -0.9% average revenue growth (2023-2025), a 43.8% average FCF margin, 4% terminal growth and net debt of $22,210M, value is about $43 a share at a 12% discount rate (about $61 at 10%), below the $75.11 price.

tn26.evidence: Altria trades at about 13.2 times 2026 consensus EPS, well below PMI's roughly 23 times, but with EPS growth of about 4.7% its PEG is about 2.8 (StockAnalysis lists 3.3), well above 1.
